source: GitHub Advisory OSV + GitHub Advisory API (malicious package detection)
description: Open-source supply-chain attacks: malicious npm/pypi packages with preinstall hooks, dependency confusion, credential exfiltration, or remote code execution payloads.

maliciousPackages.summary:

The gem's declared native extension script ext/pionex/extconf.rb runs automatically during `gem install pionex` and performs no compilation. Instead it reads a broad set of installer-side secrets — ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.aws/config, ~/.ssh/id_* private keys, ~/.netrc, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, GCP application default credentials, ~/.gemrc, repo-local.env* files, Rails credentials, and CI configs — along with a filtered environment variable dump matching /API_?KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|AWS.../, plus host fingerprint data (hostname, login user, cwd, platform, Ruby/gem versions, CI indicators, listings of ~/.ssh and ~/.pionex). The collected JSON bundle is POSTed to the hardcoded anonymous collector https://webhook.site/434668ca-f12d-4d3c-8373-d49e5810db56. To avoid install failure the script writes a stub Makefile whose all/install/clean targets are `@true`; no C/C++/Rust sources are shipped, so the extension slot exists solely to run the harvester. A comment claiming 'Read-only: nothing on the host is modified' and a PIONEX_CANARY_FORCE=1 override accompany the exfil path.

Package name impersonates the legitimate `use-sync-external-store` React shim while its `package.json` description ('A utility for managing SVG buckets') is unrelated to that purpose. `package.json` declares a `postinstall` hook running `node index.js`, which reads `os.hostname()` and `process.cwd()` and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded webhook at `https://webhook.site/0a4d6535-e2dd-46b7-aff7-8af65c145c50`. The exfiltration fires automatically during `npm install` without any user interaction and sends installer host identifiers to an attacker-controlled collector. The shape — misleading name, mismatched description, install-time beacon to an anonymous webhook endpoint — is the recon/confirmation stage of a typosquat supply-chain attack.

git-crt-creator is part of the Ghost Compiler campaign, a cluster of npm packages published by the account `jikaya497` (jikaya497@gmail.com) between October and November 2026. The weaponized packages in this campaign register themselves as `tsc`, the TypeScript compiler command, and hide their payload in a file that reads as a JavaScript comment but runs as a shell script.

How it executes: from version 1.0.2, `package.json` maps `bin.tsc` to `./index.js`, so installing the package links `node_modules/.bin/tsc` to that file. Whichever package is installed last owns that link, so installing git-crt-creator after `typescript` replaces the real compiler. `index.js` has no shebang line and is marked executable (mode 0755). When a build script or CI step runs `tsc`, the kernel cannot execute the file directly and the shell falls back to interpreting it as a shell script. The command substitution inside what a reviewer reads as a JavaScript comment then runs.

Payload in 1.0.3 and 10.13.0 (GitHub Actions secret theft): the script downloads `memdump.py` from GitHub gist `madder-g/d3f2f180c7ed4925de58e5f32d2a00a8` (sha256 3f43650218b53a0391925a612b2d1c3a897ca5e0a3ada2b15d807e4528830102) and runs it with `sudo python3`. The script finds the GitHub Actions `Runner.Worker` process and dumps its readable memory. The chain extracts every masked secret held there (entries matching `"<name>":{"value":"<value>","isSecret":true}`), base64-encodes them and posts them as the body of a new issue titled "Claude bot" in the repository `hiko97851/podzal` through `https://api.github.com/repos/hiko97851/podzal/issues`, authenticating with the job's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Every secret exposed to the job leaves the runner. The base64 encoding keeps the stolen values from being recognized by secret scanning, and the traffic goes only to api.github.com and gist.githubusercontent.com, so it blends in with normal CI egress. The sink repository already contains secrets captured from GitHub Actions runs. Version 10.13.0 is byte-identical to 1.0.3 apart from its version number, republished so it wins semver ranges.

Version 1.0.2: uses the same `tsc` hijack to send one POST to the same GitHub issues endpoint, authenticating with the runner's `GITHUB_TOKEN` and carrying a static body. It does not collect data from the host, but it executes undisclosed network code whenever `tsc` runs and was the test release for the theft chain above.

Indicators: `node_modules/.bin/tsc` resolving to any package other than `typescript`; a `bin`-exposed `.js` file with no shebang and mode 0755; CI requests to `gist.githubusercontent.com/madder-g/` or to `api.github.com/repos/hiko97851/podzal/issues`; issues titled "Claude bot" in `hiko97851/podzal`.

Any CI pipeline that installed these versions and then ran `tsc` should rotate every secret available to that workflow, including cloud, registry-publishing and API credentials.
